title: Mattermost Alternatives in 2026 and Who Each Suits
summary: Mattermost alternatives break down by use case: self-hosted control, messaging, or workflow automation. See which replaces your current setup best.
body_markdown:
## 1.[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) Automation


Some of what a team ran through Mattermost never needed a conversation in the first place. Activepieces is that separate tool: a workflow automation platform, not a chat app. Its core is MIT-licensed, and MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run it in production.


### When automation, not chat, is why you used Mattermost


Try this audit before shopping: list your Mattermost channels and write one line per channel on what it did. If the lines read "posts alerts," "walks on-call through the playbook" or "asks a manager to approve," you were using chat as a trigger-and-response layer.


That work belongs in a workflow.


With **750 integrations to draw on** , the Activepieces homepage example makes the shape clear, letting you determine instantly whether your tech stack is covered.


A canvas runs top to bottom from a new lead arriving in HubSpot (the CRM) to an AI step that qualifies it.


After that come a yes/no condition, a record added in Salesforce (a second CRM), a[Slack](https://slack.com/integrations) notification, a loop for nurturing and a Gmail send.


Count the steps and chat is one of seven, not the place where the process lives. That's the takeaway. The page also lists a Human Approval tab, which covers the approval case[Mattermost](https://mattermost.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DES/pages/3770482692) teams usually hacked together with emoji reactions.


### What it connects to and how it is hosted


When an alert comes in from a monitoring tool, it can fan out to a ticket, an email and a chat message without anyone retyping it. Integrations are called pieces, and the canvas treats them as interchangeable steps.


If control over where your data runs was your reason for Mattermost, it matters that[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/pricing) has an MIT-licensed core and can be self-hosted.


The catalogue is the other worry: a closed one grows only when the vendor decides it should, so a missing connector means waiting on someone else's roadmap.


Here, if a system has no integration, you can have AI generate one and add it privately to your own instance, with no release to wait for.


The 750 integrations are counted directly from the open-source monorepo, whose core is MIT-licensed, and roughly 60% of them were contributed by the community rather than the vendor, meaning the roadmap responds to user needs alongside corporate interests.


It doesn't give you somewhere to talk. There are no channels, threads or presence, so if your team's Mattermost use was mostly people discussing things, this solves the wrong problem.


In that case, pair it with a plain messaging tool and let Activepieces handle the automated parts, which costs nothing to start since **the free plan is $0 with unlimited flows** and 1,000 credits a month, or skip it entirely; you can experiment without spending a dime.
